observations.text: Harness display redaction: one English noun is replaced by a redaction marker in tool output at canvas_feature.body.1, canvas_feature.title, canvas_files_view.body.1, canvas_open_button.body.1 and welcome.list.1.item.3. It was not reconstructed from context. The core glossary row for that term carries the Hindi rendering कार्यक्षेत्र and six other locale renderings (espace de travail, espacio de trabajo, 工作区, рабочее пространство, không gian làm việc, ورک اسپیس), which is where the term's identity and the settled Hindi rendering are sourced; the target uses कार्यक्षेत्र in four of the five occurrences (T3 records the fifth).

The '# फ़ाइलें' lead was checked and is not in the audited bytes: no Hindi value contains '#', and the prefix-# fragment is body.1.4 ' चैट के लिए, ', so the joined sentence reads '# चैट के लिए' - matching the English 'for chats'. Likewise no chord is duplicated or invented: the chords are code spans from paletteDoorLabel() (⌘P/Ctrl+P, ⌘K/Ctrl+K, ⌘⇧P/Ctrl+Shift+P) and only the connector key repeats, three times.

Context-vs-source mismatch outside the target: welcome.image.1.alt's sidecar note says the figure shows a 'message thread' while the English value says 'message bubbles'. The Hindi follows the English value ('संदेश के बबल'), which is correct for the target; the sidecar is the stale side and this receipt does not edit it.

'memory' is rendered मेमोरी where the app means the stored memory object and याद where the English is conversational recollection ('memory of the conversation'); both are consistent with existing hi usage (ui.canvas.code_memory and ui.settings.imports use मेमोरी) and no change is requested.

'Documents' is kept Latin in the quoted example prompt (chat_input.list.1.item.1). The string is example user input naming a filesystem folder, and §1 keeps paths/names as-is; the product's Documents view itself is दस्तावेज़ elsewhere. No change requested.
